title: Typewriter and Compass
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, on the eve of revolution, Felix Ashgrove — a woman living as a man to keep her late father's type-cutting trade — works quietly in the Ashgrove print shop. When a census taker named Ilse Vantor asks one question too many, Felix's secret and Ilse's own hidden desertion from the old regime bind them together as the city erupts. To survive the victors' purge of inconvenient records, Felix must cut and print the true census ledger — including her own name, in full — before the historians' ship sails on the morning tide. They succeed at terrible cost: the shop burns, but the truth ships out, and Felix and Ilse leave together with nothing but each other and a printed page.
about_author: Zephyrine Zhou is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in coastal archive towns. Their fiction explores what ordinary hands do when history demands paperwork.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A day in the Ashgrove print shop: cutting type, mending presses, dodging neighbors' questions about why 'young master Ashgrove' never removes his gloves. Establishes the disguise, the dead father's craft, and the tightening political mood. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine competence.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Census taker Ilse Vantor arrives to verify household records and notices the ink-stained hands, the mismatched signatures, the father listed alive two years after his death. She leaves without reporting it — but returns after hours, alone. Emotional beat: the first crack in Felix's careful invisibility; wary mutual recognition.

chapters.title: What Ilse Carried
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. We learn she is a deserter from the regime's survey corps who falsified border censuses to save a village, now hiding inside the very bureaucracy hunting people like her. She offers Felix a bargain: silence for silence. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve; two secrets become one conspiracy.

chapters.title: Barricades of Paper
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Revolution ignites in the harbor quarter; printers are conscripted by both sides to produce proclamations. The Ashgrove shop becomes contested ground — its presses can legitimize whoever holds them. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering that your livelihood is a weapon others want aimed.

chapters.title: The Historians' Manifest
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse discovers the victors' provisional government has commissioned official historians sailing at week's end, authorized to burn or rewrite all pre-revolution records — including the true census that would expose both women. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the deadline is set, and it is not negotiable.

chapters.title: Cutting the Truth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix begins secretly cutting an entire alternate ledger in metal: every erased name, every falsified count, her own birth name among them. Working by candlelight while soldiers requisition the front room. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into craft; each letter cut is a small act of courage.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse's old commanding officer arrives in Vellamare reviewing census rolls and recognizes her hand in the village falsifications. He offers her amnesty if she surrenders the printer. Torn between survival and Felix, she stalls him — and realizes she has chosen. Emotional beat: love declared not in words but in refusal.

chapters.title: Night Press
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night before the ship sails, they print the true ledger under blackout conditions while the officer's men close in. The press jams; Felix bleeds over the type; Ilse holds the mob at the door with forged orders. Emotional beat: desperate intimacy — two people becoming one pair of hands.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Burning
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Climax. The officer raids the shop; the presses and the false ledgers go up in flames as Felix and Ilse flee through the print loft with the finished true ledger sewn into Ilse's coat. Felix watches her father's life's work burn and does not look back. Emotional beat: grief and liberation arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: On the Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing. At dawn they reach the harbor as the historians' ship loads; Ilse delivers the ledger openly to a junior archivist sympathetic to the record-keepers' oath. The ship sails with the truth aboard. Felix signs the passenger list with her full name for the first time. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed — identity, love, and record, all finally on the page.
